# New: Change a series' episode order after its files are imported

Part of the [custom Sonarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Sonarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/sonarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. Reviewed in [#5](https://github.com/chodeus/Sonarr/pull/5).

v5 picks an episode order (Aired, DVD, International, …) when a series is added, and Edit Series greys the setting out once the series has a file. Deleting and re-adding the series doesn't help: files are matched by the season and episode numbers in their names, so a file named in aired order lands on whichever episode holds that slot in the new order. On a long-running anime with aired and DVD orders, a re-add in DVD order would put about a quarter of the files on the wrong episode and more than a quarter on none.

Unlocking the setting isn't enough either. A refresh matches stored episodes to TVDB's by season and episode number, so switching the order rewrites every slot's metadata in place while each file stays on its old slot.

## Changes

- **Refresh matches by TVDB ID first** (`RemoteEpisodeMatcher`), then by season and episode number for the rest, so an episode TVDB moves keeps its record, file, history and monitoring. Episodes with ID 0 match by slot as before and pick up their IDs. The dedupe and field copy move out of `RefreshEpisodeService` into the same type, so the preview applies them exactly as a refresh does.
- **File seasons follow their episodes.** `EpisodeFileSeasonService` sets `EpisodeFile.SeasonNumber` to its episodes' lowest season after a refresh. Season statistics, Plex metadata, Trakt and extras read it.
- **XEM** treats a non-aired order as having no mappings, so the scene numbering left over from aired order is cleared instead of used for searches. This runs before XEM's availability checks, so an outage can't keep it in place.
- **Preview** (`GET /api/v5/series/{id}/episodeorder?seasonType=`) fetches the new order, matches it, and builds every file's new path with the rename service's own preview. Each file is `unchanged`, `renamed`, `conflict` (two files share a destination, an untracked file is there, files swap places, or it waits on a conflicted file), `unmatched` (an episode isn't in the new order by TVDB ID) or `unnameable` (a combined file whose name, read back with Sonarr's own parser, wouldn't list exactly its episodes: a gap, or episodes in two seasons). Nothing is saved.
- **Leaving aired order is refused while releases depend on it:** when XEM renumbers any of the series' episodes, or a scene title carries a real season (not the mappings' -1, "all seasons"). Other orders turn both off, so release matching would get worse.
- **`ChangeEpisodeOrder` command** runs exclusively, so no refresh can write back the series it read before the change. It reruns the preview and refuses anything the preview refuses. It saves the order without the edit event's own refresh, refreshes the series in-line, checks that every file's episodes landed where the preview said, and only then renames. If the refresh or that check fails, it puts the previous order back and refreshes again, and matching by TVDB ID moves the episodes back with their files. A file the refresh's disk scan drops because it's missing from disk no longer counts against the check. Each rename pass moves one file per free destination, so a chain moves a step at a time and no file is moved onto another. Files whose destination is taken or shared stay where they are and are reported.
- **Edit Series** enables Episode Order for series with files. Choosing another order loads the preview: a summary, Show Changes (existing → new path per file), the reason when the change is refused (refresh needed, XEM or scene titles, unmatched or unnameable files), a warning for anime orders without absolute numbers, and Rename and Move Files (on by default). Save stays disabled while the preview loads or the change is refused. The series PUT keeps the stored order and the command applies the new one.

The v5 PUT validator and the v3 API are unchanged, so a PUT still can't change the order of a series with files. On Windows the case-only rename guard in the conflict check is untested: path comparison there is case-insensitive, and the tests run on macOS.

## Tests

- `RemoteEpisodeMatcherFixture`: moved episodes, swaps, slot fallback when either ID is 0 or TVDB replaced the episode, an ID match keeping its old slot from another episode, duplicate IDs.
- `RefreshEpisodeServiceFixture`: two real Game of Thrones episodes swapping numbers keep their files.
- `EpisodeFileSeasonServiceFixture`, and `XemServiceFixture` for a non-aired order (clears scene numbering, never fetches XEM, and clears it while XEM's series list is empty).
- `EpisodeOrderChangeServiceFixture`: preview numbers and paths, nothing saved, unknown orders, unmatched and refresh-required files, each conflict kind, the XEM and scene-title refusals, and the command's refusals, save → refresh → rename order, rename off and chained renames. Combined files go through the real `RenameEpisodeFileService`, `FileNameBuilder` and parser: gapped, split across seasons, consecutive numbers in two seasons, and consecutive. A refresh that fails after a successful preview goes through the real `RefreshSeriesService` and must leave the previous order.
- `ChangeEpisodeOrderCommandFixture`: the real `CommandQueue` holds the change back while a series refresh runs, and holds a refresh back while the change runs.
- `EpisodeOrderChangeRealServicesFixture`: the whole chain below the command is real (refresh, episode refresh, disk scan, table cleanup, rename, move, transfer, scene mappings), with only SkyHook, the file system and the series and file records simulated. Episodes are rows in the test database behind the real `EpisodeService`, so the test doesn't depend on which call the refresh saves them with. It covers a file missing from disk, a chained rename across season folders that must log no errors, and all-season scene titles.
- `SkyHookProxyFixture` asserts real episodes carry a TVDB ID, since matching by ID depends on it. SkyHook v2 has sent the ID as `metadataId` and now sends it as `tvdbId`, which upstream reads; this check caught the switch.
- In Debug, 2,923 tests pass across the DataAugmentation, MediaFiles, MetadataSource, TvTests, Organizer, Messaging and Parser namespaces. Each guard was broken on purpose (48 mutations over four rounds) and its target tests failed every time.
